_about: Hard-coded constants extracted from the old Nestlyzer build (repo.html, v67/v86). Values marked _final are the effective values at runtime after all patch layers (extracted from a live headless page). Closure-scoped tables were extracted from the patch-layer source. See FEATURE_INVENTORY.md for semantics.

young_family.name: Young family
young_family.desc: Family fit. Needs family base, safety, costs and daily services. Tax alone cannot carry the result.

low_income.name: Low-income household
low_income.desc: Budget first. Favors lower housing pressure, modest tax burden, job base, safety and practical services.

low_income_family.name: Low-income family
low_income_family.desc: Cost-sensitive family profile. A place needs family base and safety before cheapness helps.

single_parent.name: Single parent
single_parent.desc: Daily reliability profile. Family base, safety, costs and services matter before tax optimization.

pensioner.name: Pensioner couple
pensioner.desc: Health, safety, taxes, calm environment and practical daily services.

single_pensioner.name: Single pensioner
single_pensioner.desc: More conservative than the couple profile. Health, safety, service base and manageable costs come first.

early_retiree.name: Early retiree
early_retiree.desc: Good services, tax position, health access and pleasant surroundings. Does not overreward remote tax pockets.

single.name: Single professional
single.desc: Jobs, real centre access, services and safety. Remote tax pockets cannot win without daily life depth.

young_professional.name: Young professional
young_professional.desc: Metro access, job base, services and safety. Remote tax advantages receive little weight.

dinks.name: DINKS
dinks.desc: Two-income lifestyle profile. Needs job depth, amenities, services and credible access to a larger centre. A highway is not enough.

remote.name: Remote worker
remote.desc: Costs, taxes, environment, safety and local services. Broadband is not joined yet.

commuter.name: Commuter
commuter.desc: Commuter profile. Uses official municipality inputs plus a visible major-city access proxy. Replace it with GTFS or road-time joins for production.

car_free.name: Car-free household
car_free.desc: Centre access and service density first. Places with weak daily access cannot win on tax or scenery.

student.name: Student
student.desc: Student profile. Uses official municipality inputs plus a visible campus-access proxy. Language area matters. Replace proxy with campus, rent and travel-time data in production.

first_home.name: First-home buyer
first_home.desc: Balances cost pressure, housing supply, safety, job base and population stability.

budget.name: Budget-constrained mover
budget.desc: Costs, housing pressure, taxes, fees and access to work matter most.

urban.name: Urban lifestyle seeker
urban.desc: Amenities, centre access, jobs, services and safety. Small remote places are gated out.

expat_professional.name: Expat professional
expat_professional.desc: Service depth, jobs, mobility, safety and lifestyle. International-school data is not joined yet.

healthcare_first.name: Healthcare-first mover
healthcare_first.desc: Health and safety-led profile with practical services and mobility as supporting factors.

nature.name: Nature-focused household
nature.desc: Open land, low crowding, safety, costs and basic services.

rural_value.name: Rural value seeker
rural_value.desc: Lower cost pressure, open land and basic service floor. Does not require city lifestyle.

hnw.name: High-net-worth mover
hnw.desc: Strict wealth shortlist. Low taxes alone cannot win without service depth, safety, health and lifestyle quality.

swiss_lottery.name: Lottery winner
swiss_lottery.desc: Wealth-preservation profile. Switzerland uses joined local tax factors; other countries show place quality separately from country-specific lottery and wealth-tax modules.

climate.name: Climate-resilient relocation
climate.desc: Environment, safety, health, costs and service base.

self_fit.name: My guided fit
self_fit.desc: A custom profile built from the self-identification questions below.

Meilen|ZH.setting: Meilen sits on the right bank of Lake Zurich, where the lakeside settlement climbs toward the Pfannenstiel ridge.
Meilen|ZH.background: Its identity is split between the old lakeside village, commuter access along the Zurichsee rail corridor, vineyards and wooded slopes above the lake.
sights: Lake Zurich shore and landing stages
Meilen|ZH.proximity: The Horgen-Meilen ferry is the cross-lake shortcut to Horgen and the left bank. Zurich, Rapperswil and the Pfannenstiel villages are the natural comparison set.
Meilen|ZH.watch: Lakeside demand can lift housing costs. Hillside addresses can mean steep walking routes. Ferry and lake access are a practical advantage, not just scenery.

Kloten|ZH.setting: Kloten is the airport municipality north of Zurich. Zurich Airport is the dominant local fact, not a footnote.
Kloten|ZH.background: The place works like an airport town: jobs, hotels, offices, logistics and rail links are stronger than in a normal municipality of similar size.
sights: Glattal connections toward Opfikon and Zurich
Kloten|ZH.proximity: Best compared with Opfikon, Rümlang, Bassersdorf and Zurich north. The airport gives access and jobs, but also aircraft noise and traffic exposure.
Kloten|ZH.watch: Aircraft noise matters by runway, flight path and time of day. Anyone sensitive to noise should inspect official noise maps before deciding.

Rümlang|ZH.setting: Rümlang sits in the Glattal next to Zurich Airport and the northern edge of Zurich city.
Rümlang|ZH.background: Its profile is shaped by airport employment, rail access and warehouse or service uses more than by classic village calm.
sights: Airport-side viewpoints and Zurich north access
Rümlang|ZH.proximity: Compare it with Kloten, Opfikon, Oberglatt and Regensdorf. Access is strong; aircraft noise and traffic need a street-level check.
Rümlang|ZH.watch: The airport is an asset and a nuisance at the same time. Noise exposure differs sharply by neighbourhood.

Opfikon|ZH.setting: Opfikon is part of the Glattal corridor between Zurich city and the airport.
Opfikon|ZH.background: Glattbrugg, office locations and rail or tram links make it a practical access municipality rather than a quiet residential retreat.
Opfikon|ZH.proximity: Compare with Zurich north, Kloten and Wallisellen. It is useful for commuters who value access over scenery.
Opfikon|ZH.watch: Traffic, airport proximity and dense development are the issues to inspect.

Altdorf|UR.setting: Altdorf is the capital of Uri in the Reuss valley, on the Gotthard north-south axis.
Altdorf|UR.background: It is historically important and locally central for Uri, with the Tell monument and old town identity, but it is not a Zurich metro lifestyle substitute.
Altdorf|UR.proximity: Compare it with Schwyz, Stans and other central Swiss valley centres. It is strong as a regional centre, not as an urban DINKS or student default.
Altdorf|UR.watch: Distance from major job, university and nightlife hubs should carry real weight for urban profiles.

Lenzburg|AG.setting: Lenzburg is a small Aargau centre between Zurich, Aarau and the lower Aare corridor.
Lenzburg|AG.background: The castle and old town give it a stronger centre feel than many municipalities of similar size, while rail and road links keep larger labour markets reachable.
Lenzburg|AG.proximity: Compare it with Aarau, Brugg, Baden and Wohlen. It can work as a practical small centre, not as a substitute for a large city.
Lenzburg|AG.watch: Check exact commute times and housing supply by neighbourhood.

Zürich|ZH.setting: Zurich is Switzerland’s largest city, on Lake Zurich and the Limmat.
Zürich|ZH.background: It combines universities, finance, culture, hospitals, lake access and the largest Swiss urban labour market. The trade-off is cost and pressure on space.
Zürich|ZH.proximity: It is the benchmark for urban Swiss profiles. Nearby alternatives usually trade access for price or space.
Zürich|ZH.watch: Housing costs and competition dominate the decision.

Zug|ZG.setting: Zug sits on Lake Zug between Zurich and central Switzerland.
Zug|ZG.background: It is known for low taxes, a compact old town, lake access and a strong business base. It is not cheap.
Zug|ZG.proximity: Compare with Baar, Cham, Risch and the Schwyz lakeside municipalities.
Zug|ZG.watch: Tax strength can mask high housing costs.

Baar|ZG.setting: Baar is the larger practical neighbour of Zug, close to Zugerberg and the Lorze corridor.
Baar|ZG.background: It offers business access and daily services with less postcard identity than Zug, but often stronger practical fit.
Baar|ZG.proximity: Compare with Zug, Cham, Steinhausen and Risch.
Baar|ZG.watch: Housing cost and local traffic should be checked.

Baden|AG.setting: Baden sits on the Limmat and is one of Aargau’s strongest historic and job centres.
Baden|AG.background: Thermal springs, old town, rail access and major employment give it a proper centre role.
Baden|AG.proximity: Compare with Wettingen, Brugg, Lenzburg and Zurich west.
Baden|AG.watch: Urban pressure and housing cost vary by neighbourhood.

Stans|NW.setting: Stans is the cantonal centre of Nidwalden below the Stanserhorn.
Stans|NW.background: It blends a historic town core, central Swiss mountain access and everyday services for the canton.
Stans|NW.proximity: Compare with Sarnen, Altdorf, Schwyz and Lucerne fringe municipalities.
Stans|NW.watch: It is a regional centre, not a large labour market.

Flurlingen|ZH.setting: Flurlingen is on the Rhine near Schaffhausen and the Rhine Falls area.
Flurlingen|ZH.background: It is small, green and river-oriented, with stronger nature and cross-border context than urban depth.
Flurlingen|ZH.proximity: Compare with Schaffhausen, Neuhausen am Rheinfall and Feuerthalen.
Flurlingen|ZH.watch: For urban profiles, check commute and job depth before being impressed by taxes or scenery.

Herrliberg|ZH.setting: Herrliberg is on Zurich’s Gold Coast, between Lake Zurich and the Pfannenstiel slope.
Herrliberg|ZH.background: Its appeal is lakeside access, hillside views, rail to Zurich and high-income residential character.
Herrliberg|ZH.proximity: Compare with Meilen, Erlenbach, Küsnacht and Zumikon.
Herrliberg|ZH.watch: Housing prices and slope access are central decision checks.

Zumikon|ZH.setting: Zumikon sits above Lake Zurich on the Forch side of the Pfannenstiel area.
Zumikon|ZH.background: It is a residential municipality with good access toward Zurich via the Forchbahn corridor and quick reach to the lake-side communities.
Zumikon|ZH.proximity: Compare with Küsnacht, Zollikon, Maur and Herrliberg.
Zumikon|ZH.watch: It is quiet and well connected, but not a dense urban centre.

ZH: Zurich is Switzerland’s deepest labour-market canton.
Lake Zurich, the Limmat valley, the Glattal and the Oberland create very different living contexts.
The right-bank Gold Coast is not the same decision as airport-side Kloten or rural Weinland.
Airport access is useful in the north, but aircraft noise matters by micro-location.
Rail access to Zurich city changes daily life more than a simple road distance.
Housing pressure is high where lake, rail and schools overlap.
For families, school route and childcare access need a local check.
For professionals, job depth and evening life are concentrated around Zurich and the Glattal.
For nature profiles, Pfannenstiel, Uetliberg, Greifensee and the Oberland are the main anchors.
Compare within subregions before comparing the canton as one block.
TI: Ticino is the Italian-speaking core of Switzerland.
Lugano is the main urban and university anchor.
Bellinzona and Locarno create different job, culture and transport patterns.
Language fit matters more here than in many score tables.
Lake, valley and mountain locations differ sharply in daily access.
Summer heat and slope exposure are real decision factors.
Cross-border context with Italy matters for labour and shopping patterns.
Public transport is stronger along the main valleys and lakes.
For students, USI makes Lugano credible, but non-Italian speakers need a language plan.
Do not compare Ticino directly with Zurich without considering language and network.
VD: Vaud combines Lausanne, Lake Geneva, Riviera towns, Jura slopes and rural hinterland.
Lausanne and EPFL/UNIL are the main student and research anchors.
Lake access often brings higher housing pressure.

TERM_DEFINITIONS_v56.tax: Tax and wealth factors. In Switzerland this includes joined municipal and cantonal tax burden fields; elsewhere tax modules must be country-specific.
TERM_DEFINITIONS_v56.jobs: Jobs and economy. Uses available official local work, workplace, income or economic scale indicators.
TERM_DEFINITIONS_v56.mobility: Mobility and connectivity. Local access and transport-related factors where joined; country packs should replace proxies with GTFS or official travel time.
TERM_DEFINITIONS_v56.safety: Safety and community. Official safety, road-safety or local proxy fields where available.
TERM_DEFINITIONS_v56.family: Education and family. School, youth, childcare or service proxies where available.
TERM_DEFINITIONS_v56.health: Health and elderly. Healthcare, age-suitability and service-depth indicators where joined.
TERM_DEFINITIONS_v56.environment: Environment and climate. Green setting, density pressure, climate or land-cover proxies where available.
TERM_DEFINITIONS_v56.affordability: Costs and affordability. Housing, tax pressure and cost proxies where available.
TERM_DEFINITIONS_v56.foundation: Foundation. Official LAU or municipality fields such as population, area, density and growth.
TERM_DEFINITIONS_v56.demographics: Demographics. Population structure, growth, age mix and household signals where joined.
TERM_DEFINITIONS_v56.commuter_access: Commuter access. A visible geographic access layer. It is not a hidden score magic field.
TERM_DEFINITIONS_v56.student_access: Campus access. A visible university and higher-education access layer. It must be replaced by official travel-time or campus data in production.
TERM_DEFINITIONS_v56.lifestyle: Lifestyle and amenities. Amenity/service depth, cultural access and local scale signals.
TERM_DEFINITIONS_v56.realestate: Real estate. Price momentum, vacancy, liquidity and housing market depth where joined.
TERM_DEFINITIONS_v56.score: Profile score, normalized to 0 to 100 from the active profile weights and available country data.
TERM_DEFINITIONS_v56.coverage: Coverage shows how much of the active profile can be scored in the selected country module.

CONFIDENCE_TEXT_v57: Confidence estimates how reliable the displayed score is for this place and profile. It combines factor coverage, source quality and whether critical inputs are official, derived or proxy. Raising the minimum confidence slider filters out places with thin or weaker data. It does not change the score of any remaining municipality.
